title: Vectors & Forces: From Direction to Dynamics
subtitle: An expanded, VR-embodied Nature of Code — every vector & force principle as a walkable room
note: Canonical tutorial spine: the perfect concept order. The single source of truth for /api/scrabble-gen?order=tutorial and the /tutorials pages. One best artifact per concept.

concepts.truth: space is a promise three numbers keep
a vector is a journey with no starting address
magnitude is how far the arrow would carry you if you walked it
to normalise is to ask "which way?" and refuse "how far?"
forces add by walking, not by counting
subtraction is the direction of the gap
a scalar is a volume knob for a direction
the dot product is how much two directions agree — and here, agreeing is mercy
projection is the part of you that lives along someone else's line
the cross product is the turn left over when two directions disagree
a field is force that has decided to be everywhere at once
motion is a vector the world keeps editing
the world only feels the part of a force that goes its way
drag is the world charging you rent on speed
a launch is a velocity you're given; gravity writes the rest
going in a circle is constant acceleration toward a centre you never reach
an orbit is two things falling toward each other and missing, forever
a spring is honest — it returns exactly what it's given, which is why it keeps time
a pendulum keeps time because the pull back is proportional to how far it's pulled
momentum is motion that refuses to be destroyed, only handed on
every bounce is a tax on a fall
a lever trades force for distance and never gets something for nothing. *(The Calder mobile is this law, drifting — every arm balanced by real weights.)*
wind is air with somewhere to be; the force is in the speed, squared
falling isn't a property of the void; it's a property of the field over it — and the field is a vector you can turn
